items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: An' they had Jimmy Rushing, me, Count Basie's band.

ctx.x: So he give me a job workin' on an assembly line. Had to pull the wires outa the motors where the crankcase go. Well, I was so young and dumb, I guess, that I'd be in the way of all that [ ] They work by piece work so they was fast, and I was too slow, so most of the time I be standin' aroun'...lookin'...'cause that's why that they said I was too slow. They couldn't make no money with me holdin' 'em up. So I left there, went back into the music business again.

So I went back to New York and started t' workin' in the night-clubs around in New York, 'cause ever'body know me there. Wasn't no trouble to get a gig. So I worked on Fifty-Second Street. I used to go down there to see Count Basie workin' in a little, small joint. So I got up an' sang a couple o' songs wit' him. So the man give me a job. An' they had Jimmy Rushing, me, Count Basie's band. So, I work around there for four...five years, an' then I took off and come back to California. I took off and run back to…

So I had to come out here, see about my place o' business. So I had my sister runnin' it for me. 'Course, in the meantime, I went to Chicago. I lived seventeen years in Chicago. I got married in Chicago to a lady called Louella Brown. So we got together...Cut it off [the tape recorder].
